newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai baht, U.S. rates see Singapore stock end down.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht, U.S. rates see Singapore stock end down.

text.p: Selling prompted by Thailand's currency crisis saw Singapore shares end weaker on Friday, with dealers predicting a sidelining of investor interest until after Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC) meeting.
"Concerns about Thai exposures have pushed the market down and I don't think anybody will be buying much before the FOMC next week," one dealer at a local broking house said.

The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed down 9.24 at 2,060.50, a more muted fall than Thursday's 28-point plunge prompted by the speculative attacks on the Thai baht, but nevertheless hit by further fallout on Friday.
Market volume was a thinnish 135.1 million shares with gainers beating losers 204 to 140.
City Developments led the falls, down Singapore $0.60 at S$12.70. Fraser & Neave lost S$0.30 to S$11.50 and UOB bank dropped S$0.25 to S$8.40.
Gains were topped by Creative Technology, up S$0.80 at S$26.90 while North Borneo Timber jumped S$0.70 to S$11.70.
Over the counter traded MBF Capital was the day's most active stock with 11.2 million units moving on market talk about a possible merger deal. The share closed up S$0.19 at S$2.44.
